trace.top_explanation:
The 6-14 s silence right after the parse call is best explained by about 50 blocking Upstash reads that run back-to-back on the loop. The largest share, 18-36 per compare, are Shopify catalog reads that none of the existing flags covers. All file:line references are at 7b224c5a.

**What runs straight after parse.** `_compare_from_text_impl` starts three things at scs:4116-4126:
- the profile task, which does two Supabase selects inline: scs:5441 (run_db is inline because ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is OFF) and database_service.py:892-896 (no flag at all);
- the two `_fetch_product_data` calls.

**Before each task's first real await**, every product does the following synchronously:
- 4 Upstash GETs: specs and reviews (scs:5617-5618), price L1 (scs:6498), negcache (scs:6586);
- 1 Supabase L2 price select (scs:6513);
- up to 6 `httpx.AsyncClient` constructions: unified search, 4 discovery searches at scs:6787-6801, and shopping.

**The Shopify chain.** `_get_price` also starts the speculative adapter prefetch (scs:6888-6990). Every Shopify and gcc-Shopify source runs `fetch_shopify_price` -> `_fetch_shopify_catalog`, and that function's first action is a sync `get_cached('shopify_catalog:<domain>')` (price_service.py:15159). On a hit it returns the cached 250-product catalog with no await, then matches it on the loop. On a negcache hit it returns the sentinel, also with no await. So the whole chain runs serially and silently, because httpx logs at WARNING (logging_config.py:47).

**Source counts.** I counted these from the shipped catalog with ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES on:

| Category | Sources per product | Catalog GETs per compare |
|---|---|---|
| electronics | 9 | 18 |
| makeup | 14 | 28 |
| other | 14 | 28 |
| fragrances | 18 | 36 |

Adding the Algolia, sitemap, noon and unbxd breaker and config GETs, the burst comes to about 30-55 Upstash calls. At 90-200 ms each that is 2.7-11 s. The four Supabase calls add 0.5-1.8 s and up to 12 client constructions add 0.1-2.6 s. That makes roughly 3.3-15 s, which matches loop_lag 6.5 s, 14.8 s all-time, /health timing out at 5 s, and the catalog-heavy categories (fragrances, beauty, other) being worst.

**How the other symptoms follow.**
- The woo adapters' curl calls run in threads (woocommerce_service.py:340). They finish during the block, and their callbacks all run in the same millisecond once the loop frees up.
- The Serper shopping and unified-search connects were started before the block. Their 8 s connect deadline expires while the loop is blocked, so httpx reports ConnectTimeout even though the network answers in 2-12 ms. That gives the 12-21 s serper_shopping stage, the Bright Data fallback (breaker open, plus 1 more GET), and gather-stage hard-cap PARTIALs.

**Flipping every existing flag would not fix it.**
- ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD would move about 8 of the burst calls.
- ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD would move 3 of the 4 Supabase calls; demographics has no flag.
- The Shopify catalog get/set, sitemap buckets, Algolia/noon/unbxd breaker calls, negcache read, reviews get/set, tier-15 counters, image credit, rating record_usage, the Bright Data gate and model_router all call `cache_service` directly, and no flag covers them.

**Later and secondary contributors.**
- BeautifulSoup parses are 0.3-2.5 s per page with up to 4 passes when ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD is OFF, but they mostly come after the shopping stage.
- Inline getaddrinfo is under 90 ms per call (ENABLE_OFFLOOP_DNS_RESOLVE).
- The pre-parse route gate costs 2 create_client calls (ENABLE_SUPABASE_CLIENT_REUSE) and 4-5 executes.
- About 12-18 post-response persistence writes block the loop after the reply.
- The unbounded Upstash transport can add a 3 s sleep on any failed call (ENABLE_UPSTASH_BOUNDED_TRANSPORT, needs a restart).

**UNVERIFIED:**
- Cached catalog payload sizes, and whether the catalogs sit in Upstash as full catalogs or as 429 negcache sentinels. Check `shopify_catalog:*` key sizes read-only, and grep the logs for "Redis SET error".
- The AsyncClient construction cost on prod Linux.
- Whether SERPER_API_KEYS holds 2 or more keys, which would add 1 GET per key per Serper call (serper_service.py:158-184).
- The burn-sentinel GET, which depends on the lifetime counter.
- The categories of the six curated pairs.

flags.read_per_call_or_restart: Read per call. offloop_dns_enabled() calls os.getenv on every call (app/utils/url_validator.py:130-134), and the single dispatcher checks it each time (url_validator.py:526-537). Its knobs are not all per call. DNS_RESOLVER_POOL_SIZE (default 16, clamped 1..64) is read once, when the dns-resolve pool is first built (url_validator.py:147-165, :168-184), so changing it needs a restart. DNS_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 2.0) is read per call (:137-144).
flags.preconditions: The docs give this flag no code precondition. It is step (1) of the W0 ACTIVATION ORDER, flipped alone with one canary per step and never batched (CLAUDE.md:419; also CLAUDE.md:658 and :677, and READINESS_BACKEND.md:199, which sets the canary as 3 app-shaped compares then /health loop_lag_max_60s_ms < 1000). It needs the owner's explicit yes (owner W0 re-decision B: CRITIQUE_ENG_OPS.md:60, session-74 NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md:26). The FANOUT rulings list it as a candidate flip window after canary 7 (PR_344_FANOUT_BODY.md:21, FABLE_RULINGS_FANOUT_STARVE.md:23). MET in code: W0-1 and W0-1b are merged. The dedicated pool is not the qaren-worker executor (url_validator.py:168-184). The memo holds confirmed negatives only (:355-370, :509-513). A queued resolve that never started is not memoised (:478-505). All 11 call sites go through _validate_url_offloop_or_sync: url_routes.py:296/317/359/381/402/421, price_service.py:14843/14864, shopify_pdp_service.py:319, url_extraction_service.py:115/125. The canary-7 baseline exists per the measured facts.
flags.risks_when_on: (1) Fail-closed on a 2 s bound. A started resolve slower than 2 s writes a 60 s negative memo for that host, so a healthy but slow storefront drops off the price path for 60 s (url_validator.py:460-475). Measured DNS for all 36 retailer hosts is under 90 ms, so this should be rare. (2) Pool saturation. The fan-out runs about 10-20 concurrent validations per compare plus redirect hops against 16 workers. A resolve queued past 2 s fails closed for that call only (not memoised, :478-505), which costs capture without a log-visible host verdict. (3) getaddrinfo cannot be cancelled. Zombie threads are bounded by the pool, but the threads are non-daemon, so one parked resolve can delay process shutdown by the OS resolver timeout (CLAUDE.md:414). (4) Successful resolves are never memoised (the rebinding guard), so repeat positive lookups get no faster. The gain is that the resolve leaves the loop, not that it gets cheaper. Expected loop-lag gain: modest in steady state (under 90 ms per resolve, per URL and per hop), but it removes the 11-12 s per-black-holed-host freeze on /url/* and the price path.
flags.canary_signal: /health loop_lag_max_60s_ms after 3 app-shaped compares (target under 1000 per READINESS_BACKEND.md:199). The /url/* 400 rate. Railway drain time on the next deploy. Log lines to watch: '[SSRF] dedicated DNS resolver pool created: max_workers=16' (url_validator.py:180-182, should appear once per process); '[SSRF] DNS resolve queued past the 2.0s bound' or 'started only ... before the bound' (pool saturation, :483-505), which should be about zero; '[SSRF] DNS resolve exceeded 2.0s' (:467-471). Also the per-compare count of price sources and PASS/PARTIAL against canary 7a (capture must not drop), and the count of Serper httpx ConnectTimeouts per compare.
flags.rollback: Unset or false the variable on web. It takes effect on the next call with no restart, and flag OFF is byte-identical: the memo is not read or written (url_validator.py:349-353, :427-432), and _validate_url_offloop_or_sync calls the sync validator inline (:536-537). The already-built pool stays idle until the process restarts. To change the pool size, use DNS_RESOLVER_POOL_SIZE plus a restart.

Three copies of the helper exist: price_service.py:4300-4320, structured_comparison_service.py:1646-1652 and url_extraction_service.py:387-392, each calling os.getenv. Its knob PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS (default 4, clamped 1..16) is read once, when the price-parse pool is first built (price_service.py:4365-4375, :4377-4391; CLAUDE.md:459), so resizing needs a restart.
flags.preconditions: It is step (2) of the W0 order: ENABLE_OFFLOOP_DNS_RESOLVE must be ACTIVE and stable first, one canary per step (CLAUDE.md:419). The docs also say to size PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS for the box. MET in code: R-W04 #196 and W0-4e/f/g are merged. The soup is built once and threaded through the JSON-LD passes. The bounded pool sits behind a per-loop semaphore acquired before submit (price_service.py:4394-4440), and the contextvars copy is in place (:4433-4436). The PRICE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES 3,000,000 cap is at :4326, and /health exposes price_parse_pool (main.py:271-282, :598). The corpus gate showed 0/1656 differing ON vs OFF (CLAUDE.md:417). NOT MET at head: the ordering precondition, because DNS is OFF.
flags.risks_when_on: (1) The parse leaves the loop but still holds the GIL, because html.parser is pure Python. The measured residual is 35-143 ms per large page, and 171-534 ms with six large pages at once (CLAUDE.md:417), so it bounds the lag rather than removing it. (2) Four workers queue parses in asyncio. Under the 15 s price race and the 30 s hard cap, the queue wait adds wall-clock and could turn into more SLOW-MISS or TIMEOUT drops if the pool is too small for the BH_GCC fan-out (about 30 sources per compare). (3) A parse whose await was cancelled by a wait_for cap keeps its pool thread while its semaphore slot is released, so pool occupancy is under-reported (price_service.py:4346-4362). (4) Stated limit: with the flag ON, the 3 MB cap also truncates _lazy_bh_pdp_backfill's regex scan (W0-4e, CLAUDE.md:417). Expected gain, an INFERENCE that is UNVERIFIED: this is the largest single loop-lag reducer. Inline parses measured 300-602 ms each with a 50 ms heartbeat ticking 0 times (CLAUDE.md:417), and a cold compare runs many of them at fetch_page_price, the firecrawl/scrapedo scrapers, iHerb/Bolo/Boutiqaat/pharmacy and SCS._fetch_page_price. That matches the 10-14 s silence after the parse LLM call, after which the queued woo callbacks all log in the same millisecond.

It should appear only after the first flagged parse, and workers should be 4. A queued value that persists across polls means orphaned parses. /health loop_lag_max_60s_ms should fall well below the 6546 ms baseline. The log line '[PRICE-PARSE] pool built workers=4' should appear once. The woo-adapter results should stop logging in one millisecond, and the post-parse silence should shrink. Serper ConnectTimeouts per compare should drop, because the httpx connect timer can no longer expire behind a blocked loop. Compare outcomes against canary 7a: PARTIAL count, partial_stage, and price-source count, where any drop points to pool queueing.

verdict.summary:
I re-derived both reports from the code at 7b224c5a and both hold on substance, with the corrections below.

**Trace report: confirmed.** The Shopify catalog read at price_service.py:15159 is a synchronous Upstash GET with no await before it, so every Shopify and gcc-Shopify source in the speculative prefetch (scs:6888-6990) runs one after another on the event loop. I recounted the sources by importing source_router from a git-archive snapshot of 7b224c5a with ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES=true, and the per-category counts match exactly: 18-36 catalog GETs per compare. No existing flag covers these, or the reads of sitemap metadata and buckets, the Algolia/noon/unbxd breaker checks, the negcache entry, the reviews L1 cache or the Serper exhausted-key GETs.

**Trace corrections:**
- Several line numbers have drifted: scs:6883, scs:6829, scs:5621-5622 and scs:8760/8857/8886. logging_config is at app/middleware/logging_config.py:47.
- Its statement that page parsing plays no part in the post-parse stall goes too far. The bolo and boutiqaat sitemap adapters parse their product pages on the loop inside that same prefetch window, for the beauty categories, when the sitemap index is warm.

**Safety report: flag semantics confirmed.** Per-call vs restart behaviour, the two doc discrepancies (http2 at CLAUDE.md:415, the stale half-open precondition at CLAUDE.md:384, resolved in code by #115), and the drain merge with its on-deploy check still owed all check out.

**Safety corrections:**
- The claim that ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD is the largest loop-lag win and explains the 10-14 s silence is unverified, and the trace contradicts it. It keeps step 2 only because CLAUDE.md:419 fixes the order.
- The DNS flag has a risk the report misses. While the loop stalls for more than 2 s on the uncovered Upstash calls, a lookup that has already finished can still hit its 2 s timeout and fail closed, logging "DNS resolve exceeded". This is an inference about event-loop ordering, plausible but not measured. The 60 s negative memo is dropped immediately, so the cost is one skipped product-page fetch per call.
- The absolute canary bar (loop_lag under 1000 ms) cannot be met at any step while the uncovered sites remain. It needs an owner ruling to judge each step against canary 7a instead.
- Two small fixes on ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD: offloaded calls share one memoised client with the library's 120 s timeout; they do not build a client per thread. The flag also depends on the shutdown drain for background persistence writes.

**Final order:** the documented order stands. DNS needs the owner's explicit yes. Then PARSE, then SUPABASE_REUSE, then UPSTASH_BOUNDED (needs a restart; verify the drain lines on that redeploy). Then SYNC_DB, then ASYNC_REDIS last, after the drain is verified and the stale CLAUDE.md:384 row is corrected or ruled on. One flag per window, all flips by the owner.

The main stall itself needs a new code unit that moves the uncovered Upstash calls off the loop. None of the six flags removes it.
